uncertainties.note: Clipped nickname of the Siberian Railway rendered 'Sibe-Rail' (project coinage, no official English found). Fallback is the full 'Siberian Railway' (locked). Row 2000 is in batch_01975.
'Gauli Team' follows English Wikipedia; character glossary role text says 'Gauli Squad' (not a locked term entry; 'Team' also avoids the missing q glyph).

Exchange aboard an unnamed ship that treats the Gekko's arrival as news and is asked for support by the Siberian Railway: a captain and a subordinate who owns the quoted 'cargo'. Speakers and the nature of the cargo are not identified in the table; 1917's verb could mean the captain personally sortieing or the ship launching its forces - 'sortie' kept. 1920 kept passive because the subject is omitted.
Form of address for the player-side reinforcements rendered 'helpers'; a friendlier/more natural alternative ('reinforcements', 'friends') may be preferred for consistency by the reviewer.
Verb unsaid in source ('Why are you...'); left open rather than adding 'here' or 'fighting'.
Object 'him' with verb omitted; 'why bring him along' infers the verb from Gain's reply in 1915 (he got him involved).
Speaker not identifiable (uses a harsh 'you'); sits between Sara's 1932 and Gainer's 1934. Kept speaker-neutral.
Source says only 'found!'; read as the friendly operator reacting to enemy lines 1942-1945 (train discovered). 'It's been spotted' keeps the object loose.
'Too late. This is our win.' - which side says it is unclear (timer-expiry line from an enemy, or a friendly line when the train escapes). Feminine speech style in source.
Failure line; whether the rebuke is aimed at the listener ('you') or third parties is not stated.
Banter between two unidentified trigger-happy pilots (probably a player-side pilot and Gain or another guest); no identities assigned. 1963/1964 are one sentence split over two rows.
1969 names Eureka as sitting beside the speaker, so that speaker is Renton (male, glossary); the complaining partner is unidentified.
1973-1974 'we left the military' in feminine speech - a Gekkostate member (likely Talho) but not tagged; translation is speaker-neutral.
